newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Capital inflows a challenge for Asia-Camdessus.
newsitem.headline: Capital inflows a challenge for Asia-Camdessus.

text.p: Capital inflows and the quickening pace of financial integration and innovation pose fresh challenges to Asian economies, Michel Camdessus, managing director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), said on Friday.

"The presence of large capital inflows reduces the room for policy manoeuvre and limits the scope for policy mistakes," Camdessus told a joint IMF-Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) conference in the British colony.

"Moreover financial sector reforms and increased access to international markets expose domestic financial systems to new risk. In many countries in Asia and elsewhere, prudential regulation and supervision have not kept pace with the new complexities of banking business."
He said there was no substitute for stable macroeconomic policies that give confidence to financial markets and attract private savings,

"Likewise transparent and predictable regulatory policies and a reliable legal framework are essential ingredients in creating a favourable investment climate," he said. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843-6352
